text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Police led by deputy interior minister Agim Shehu fights protestors in the southern city of Vlore, the army shoots in the air, 20 people injured during the clashes, among them a journalist.

- Editorial says unlike Serbia's Milosevic and the Bulgarian Socialists, Albania's President Sali Berisha tells radio interview he will "never" give in which means he is responsible for the many frauds seen in recent years.
- Police blocked the printing and later the distribution of the Koha Jone daily in one district.

- Opposition says the people in Serbia and Bulgaria are sovereign but not in Albania where the ruling party, although not a political dictatorship, has a fascist face frightening people with the police and security forces.

- The small right-wing National Front party threatens to boycott parliament after the recent behaviour of the ruling party and President Sali Berisha. Its branch in Vlore withdrew its members from the district's local assembly.
- Only 4,000 depositors have received partial refunds of their capital from two failed pyramid schemes.
- Creditors of the bankrupt Sude pyramid scheme have created a commission to see how to get their capital back.
- Soccer matches will not be held again this weekend because of the present tense situation.
- People in Vlore protested all day on Wednesday and clashed with police.
- Chaos in the bank booths where depositors are meant to receive refunds from two failed pyramid schemes. Many refuse to accept only a partial refund, no one wants bank certificates.
